backingModelNote: Authoritative backing semantics are stated in NudgeRatchet._dispatch comments (lines 64-100): the hook accrues phUSD mint-debt against the GROSS dispatched `amount`; the actual prime is forwarded to an EXTERNAL batchMinter/recipient sink (or, for poolers, retained as protocol-owned LP). The intended invariant is debt(phUSD) <= value-retained-by-protocol, i.e. surplus = over-backing is SAFE. Ledger DEDUP-001 ('phUSD unbacked mint, owner-driven, out-of-scope external backing model') confirms the cross-contract/off-chain backing reconciliation is intentionally external and out of scope. Findings below are evaluated against THIS model, not against an idealized 1:1 on-chain reserve.

findings.verdict: REFUTED (no on-chain double-mint; consistent with intended external backing model)
findings.description: Investigated whether the donationSplit% prime forwarded to `recipient` (the BalancerPooler batch-minter) accrues a SECOND phUSD debt on another dispatcher/hook while UniboostMintDebtHook already accrued debt on the GROSS amount -> double-minting unbacked phUSD.
findings.valueFlowPath: NFTMinterV2 transferFrom prime -> Uniboost.dispatch -> _dispatch: (a) safeTransfer(recipient, amount*donationSplit/100) to EXTERNAL sink; (b) retained (100-donationSplit)% stays on Uniboost for pool(). Base then calls UniboostMintDebtHook.onDispatch(GROSS amount) -> mintDebt += amount*scale*ratio/100. pull() later mints that phUSD to the hook's recipient.
findings.analysis: The donation `recipient` is an EXTERNAL address (intended: an off-chain/external batch-minter). It is NOT an in-scope ITokenDispatcherV2 and does NOT call any dispatcher's onDispatch. The donated prime therefore accrues NO second on-chain phUSD debt anywhere in scope. There is exactly ONE debt accrual per dispatch (UniboostMintDebtHook), on the gross amount, bounded by ratio<=50. No on-chain path forwards the donated prime back into a second hook. The cross-contract double-mint hypothesis does not hold for the in-scope contracts.
findings.economicImpact: None on-chain. If an external batch-minter ALSO mints phUSD against the same donated prime, that is the documented external/off-chain backing reconciliation already captured by suppressed DEDUP-001 (out-of-scope external backing model) and is an operational accounting concern for the off-chain minter, not an in-scope contract bug.

findings.verdict: REFUTED as under-backing; debt is conservatively bounded vs retained value. Volatility-of-LP nuance noted (see ECON-004).
findings.description: Debt accrues = amount*scale*ratio/100 on GROSS prime, but pool() later SWAPS the retained prime into a volatile UniV2 LP position. Assessed whether phUSD ends up over- or under-backed and whether ratio<=50 bounds it.
findings.valueFlowPath: Gross prime P dispatched. Debt = (ratio/100)*P phUSD (in value terms, for a $1 prime: <= $0.50). Retained value: donation D = (donationSplit/100)*P -> external sink (held as prime/USDC), plus R = (1-donationSplit/100)*P -> swapped to pair, half to target, added as LP -> POL held on Uniboost. Total protocol-retained gross value at dispatch time = D + R = P (minus only swap/MEV friction at pool() time).
findings.analysis: At dispatch, the ENTIRE prime amount P is preserved as protocol-controlled value: the donation portion sits in the external sink and the retained portion is (later) converted to POL LP held on the dispatcher (recoverable via rescueERC20). Debt minted via pull() is at most (ratio/100)*P. Since ratio is hard-bounded ratio<=50 (MAX_RATIO=50, setRatio reverts only on >50), debt <= 0.5*P while retained value ~= P. This is a >=2:1 collateralization buffer at dispatch. The mint-debt is therefore conservatively OVER-backed in nominal terms, matching the intended 'surplus is safe / over-backing' model. ratio<=50 does bound this conservatively. The pool() swap converts the retained backing from prime into LP, but the buffer (2x) is wide enough to absorb LP price drift for the targetToken/pairToken before the pull() mint would exceed retained value; quantifying that drawdown is a solvency-monitoring concern, not an arithmetic bug.
findings.economicImpact: No structural under-backing introduced by pooling. The backing asset CHANGES KIND (prime -> volatile LP) for the retained portion, so the 2x nominal buffer is the protection against LP depreciation. If targetToken collapses >~50% relative to the debt denomination AND donationSplit is low (most value is in LP), the LP could in principle back less than the accrued debt -- but this requires a large adverse price move on a protocol-owned, owner-recoverable LP position and the debt is realized by owner/recipient pull(), not user-redeemable 1:1. Not a direct theft path.
findings.profitability: No attacker-extractable profit; this is a passive solvency/over-collateralization observation.

findings.verdict: VALID but Low (operator-triggered, bounded by min params, POL-only) - mirror of open ledger L-06.
findings.description: pool() performs two router swaps (prime->pair with minPairOut, half pair->target with minTargetOut) and addLiquidity(...,0,0,...). deadline=block.timestamp gives no real deadline protection; addLiquidity amountAMin/amountBMin are hardcoded 0. Value leaks to MEV (sandwich/JIT) on each pooling event.
findings.codeSnippet: router.addLiquidity(targetToken, _pairToken, targetBal, pairRemaining, 0, 0, address(this), block.timestamp); require(liquidity >= minLP, ...);
findings.valueFlowPath: Retained prime -> swap1 (prime->pair) -> swap2 (pair->target) -> addLiquidity. Each step is a public mempool tx subject to sandwiching; the addLiquidity 0/0 mins mean ratio-imbalance is unprotected at the router layer, relying solely on the post-call minLP require and the two upstream swap floors.
findings.analysis: Slippage protection is THREE pooler-supplied floors: minPairOut, minTargetOut, and a post-call minLP require. The addLiquidity 0/0 mins are a known UniV2-router limitation (the router has no min-liquidity param) and are backstopped by minLP. As long as the authorized pooler computes tight floors off-chain, leakage is bounded. The residual risks are: (1) deadline=block.timestamp offers no protection against a validator holding the tx for a later, manipulated block; (2) two sequential swaps compound sandwich exposure; (3) if the pooler passes lax floors (0 or stale), value leaks to MEV. The loss is borne by the protocol's own POL (retained prime being converted to LP), NOT by end users, and pool() is permissioned (onlyAuthorizedPooler). This is the exact shape and severity of open ledger L-06 (BalancerPoolerV2 pool() single-sided LP-add relying on off-chain keeper minBPT) and prior L-03; severity stays Low for the same reasons (operator-triggered, not user-facing, bounded by operator-chosen floors).
findings.economicImpact: MEV extraction of a bounded fraction of each pooled batch from protocol-owned liquidity. Bounded by the three pooler-supplied floors; zero if floors are tight.
findings.attackScenario: 1. Authorized pooler calls pool() with loose/zero minPairOut/minTargetOut/minLP (operational error). 2. MEV bot sandwiches the prime->pair and pair->target swaps. 3. Protocol receives less LP than fair value; the delta is extracted. Requires lax floors; tight floors reduce leak to dust.
findings.profitability: Profitable for MEV only when pooler floors are loose relative to true output and pooled size > gas. Not profitable against tight floors.
findings.dedupHint: Same root cause class as ledger L-06 (open) and L-03 (fixed-Balancer-variant). Likely DEDUP/merge with L-06 as the Uniboost instance of the keeper-min-param-only LP-add pattern. Should NOT be escalated above Low.

findings.verdict: VALID coupling-gap footgun at Low - direct mirror of open ledger L-05 (Balancer batchDonationSize vs Hook.ratio decoupling). Edge cases 0%/100% are SAFE.
findings.description: donationSplit (on Uniboost) and ratio (on UniboostMintDebtHook) are two independently owner-set parameters in two separate contracts with NO on-chain coupling. Debt always accrues on GROSS amount (debt = ratio% of P) while only donationSplit% of P leaves to the external sink and the rest becomes POL LP. Examined edge cases (0%, 100%), rounding, and whether debt-on-gross-while-forwarding-part creates an accounting gap.
findings.valueFlowPath: setDonationSplit(0..100) and Hook.setRatio(0..50) are decoupled. Debt = (ratio/100)*P. Sink-backing = (donationSplit/100)*P. POL-backing = (1-donationSplit/100)*P (as LP). Total backing = P regardless of donationSplit.
findings.analysis: EDGE CASES: (a) donationSplit=0: nothing leaves to the sink; the entire P is retained and pooled to LP; debt = ratio%*P <= 50%*P is fully backed by POL LP. SAFE. (b) donationSplit=100: the entire P is safeTransferred to the external sink; pool() later reverts 'nothing to pool' (amountIn==0) which is benign (no LP formed, no value lost on-chain); debt = ratio%*P <= 50%*P is backed by the sink donation (which is 100%*P >= debt). SAFE. (c) ROUNDING: donationAmount = (amount*donationSplit)/100 floors; the un-donated remainder (incl. the rounding dust) stays on-contract and is swept into the next pool() -- no prime is lost. debt = (amount*scale*ratio)/100 also floors (sub-wei dust accrues to protocol, never over-credits) -- this is the profiler's VERIFIED rounding direction. No accounting gap from rounding. ACCOUNTING GAP CHECK: debt-on-gross while forwarding only part is NOT under-backing because the un-forwarded part is retained as POL LP, not lost (see ECON-002). The real residual issue is the SAME as open ledger L-05: there is no on-chain invariant ensuring ratio <= effective backing coverage, so a non-obvious owner mis-set (e.g. ratio raised, donationSplit changed, or hook ratio diverging from the sibling's intended coverage) could in principle let accrued debt outrun the kind/liquidity of retained backing without any contract reverting. Because ratio is hard-capped at 50 and total retained value ~= P, the worst case stays at <=50% debt vs ~100% retained value, so the coupling gap is a transparency/footgun issue, not a solvency break.
findings.economicImpact: No direct loss. Coupling-gap footgun: the two-parameter, two-contract design means correct backing relies on the owner setting ratio and donationSplit coherently, with no on-chain guard. Surfaced as an operational hazard (Law 3 non-obvious footgun) consistent with how L-05 was rated.
findings.attackScenario: Not an attack; a non-obvious owner footgun. Owner sets Hook.ratio independent of Uniboost.donationSplit; nothing reverts; over time the realized phUSD (via pull) could be backed by a volatile-LP-heavy or sink-heavy mix the owner did not intend. Bounded by ratio<=50.
findings.dedupHint: Direct Uniboost mirror of open ledger L-05 (BalancerPoolerV2 batchDonationSize <-> Hook.ratio decoupling). Should DEDUP/merge with L-05 as the same root-cause class, Low. Also relates to L-02 (setRatio==MAX_RATIO inclusive comment/code mismatch) already in ledger.

summary.note: ECON-003 and ECON-004 are Uniboost mirrors of already-open ledger Lows (L-06 and L-05 respectively) and should reconcile to those root-cause classes rather than count as new Highs/Mediums. ECON-001 and ECON-002 (the high-priority double-mint / under-backing leads) are REFUTED on-chain: single debt accrual per dispatch on gross amount, total retained value ~= P, debt bounded by ratio<=50 (>=2x buffer). The external batch-minter backing reconciliation remains the intentionally out-of-scope concern captured by suppressed DEDUP-001.
